answer: Under birthday-bond admission, each joining identity posts a refundable 50-token bond and publishes a hash whose first h=6 hex digits differ from every identity admitted that epoch; a prefix collision confiscates both bonds. A gale of fake agents fails fast: m identities collide with probability roughly m²/16⁶, so 100 sybils face near-certain forfeiture, costing 5,000 tokens versus one honest bond of 50 at the horizon of 10,000 identities, where collisions stay rare. Attackers pay quadratically while honest agents whisper past with one deposit, refunded after the epoch closes.
